about.title: About Me
about.previewText1: I build things for the web. On the product side, I've shipped real-time chat systems, ride-sharing applications, and e-commerce platforms. On the side, I tinker with Linux, writing PyTorch models, and open-source tooling — mostly because I find them interesting.
about.previewText2: I write TypeScript, prefer boring and correct over clever and broken, and I like working on projects where the code directly affects how something feels to use.
about.pageIntro: Hi, I'm Parsa. I like building things for the web. I work across the full stack — from React UIs to distributed backends — and spend a good chunk of my free time on personal R&D: Linux, AI models, and playing with open-source stuff.
about.startedP1: I started programming when I wanted to build tools for myself in comparison to using heavy, generic software that didn't fit my workflow. The itch to optimize existing systems led me down the rabbit hole of computer science.
about.startedP2: For a while that meant neural networks and ML — training models, reading papers, the academic side of things. But most people building real products needed websites, and if they wanted ML, it was as a backend service (like counting hair follicles in a test vial from uploaded photos, vectorizing the data, and serving predictions back to the UI) rather than a research project. So I moved into web development. Turns out a full stack has enough moving parts to stay interesting.
about.startedP3: Since then, I've worked both solo and in teams of up to 7+ engineers. On the product side, I've designed e-commerce websites, scaled location tracking infrastructure for GPS-tracking systems, and built real-time chat applications.
about.rdP1: Beyond product engineering, I love digging into algorithms. I've trained custom VAEs to detect geological mineral zones in highly imbalanced spectroscopic data, and CNNs to recognize labeled data.
about.philosophyP1: I believe code should be written for humans to read first. That means TypeScript as a default, avoiding over-abstraction, and actually profiling before assuming something is slow.
about.philosophyP2: I can take a product from a description to a deployed stack — database schema, API, UI, and everything in between. I like projects where the engineering decisions visibly affect the end result.
